classification: test-gate integration; existing production SystemBackup/SystemRestore config+kubecli APIs unchanged
scope: Single-cluster reconstruction of absent Volume/PV/PVC from an external full backup and disabled-policy resource package, original namespace preserved; not an independent DR site or full data-protection module
conclusions: restoreVolumes uses the bundled LastBackup for a missing non-standby volume. Existing objects are not rolled back. Data point is the backup time, not the bundle time.
All existing volumes must be detached. Preserve exact external package and every full-backup referenced object before and after deleting original UID-bound source objects.
SystemRestore creates longhorn-system-rollout-NAME Job with a controller ownerReference to the SystemRestore UID. Its Pods must bind to the actual Job UID and complete successfully.
PV recreation waits until native data restore is finished, clears the original ClaimRef, and PVC recreation binds the original PV name in the pre-existing namespace. Volume/PV/PVC get new API UIDs.

Reconstructed objects use longhorn.io/last-system-restored and -at; Volume additionally records longhorn.io/last-system-restored-backup. Existing shared resources can receive last-skipped-system-restored annotations.

Deleting SystemRestore aborts its Job and remaining rollout, without transactional rollback. Unverified recovery preserves source package, volume backup, target resources, private ledger and external store.

restorePersistentVolumeClaims returns after API creation; Kubernetes PVC/PV binding converges asynchronously. Completed rollout must be followed by a bounded binding/data-restore wait, then strict UID/provenance/capacity checks. This integration assumption was corrected before any remote launch.

GetSystemBackupURL uses filepath.Join on getSystemBackupURI, removing its trailing slash; the exact last-system-restored annotation is therefore the target plus backupstore/system-backups/v1.12.1/name without a trailing slash. A failure from assuming the URI helper output equals the final URL is archived separately as a test-gate defect, not a product failure.
fixture_boundary: Original .146-.148 leased V2 baseline; one random 2Gi three-replica source, own namespace/clients, own full backup/snapshot and resource bundle, precise restore Job/Pod chain, independent TLS object-store fixture. No raw disk wipe or shared cluster replacement.
cleanup_scope: After verified business recovery, retire original-UID restore and Job/Pods, resource bundle, current-UID business objects and exact original backup/BackupVolume; full namespace graph permits historical UIDs only for original Events. Restore target/credentials and store, verify original raw-disk and core identities. Unconfirmed or unverified restore stops cleanup and preserves material.
